newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 12.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The increasing trade deficit is the largest problem with the Czech economy today. Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated this yesterday and added that one of the main negative influences on the deficit is the fact that domestic companies do not cooperate.
- According to many observers of the cabinet, it is possible that due to disputes inside the coalition, the cabinet may not reach a decision today on how energy prices and rents will increase.

- The investment company Harvard Capital & Consulting may be allowed to transform its closed-end funds to open, after a meeting with the Finance Ministry yesterday, Ludmila Nutilova, spokeswoman for the ministry, said.

PRAVO - Justice Minister Vlasta Parkanova announced on Tuesday that she will present a proposal to remove the highest government attourny, Bohumira Kopecna, from her position. She refused to give any further information.
- Drug distributors are suing another five hospitals which owe more than 300 million crowns past the deadline for payment.
- Pro Win, which owns Bohemia Art s.r.o., made an agreement with one of Bohemia Art's creditors, Ligna, on Monday that it will pay debts of 13 million crowns by the middle of the year.
- About 150,000 people in the Czech Republic, primarily between the ages of 15 and 19, use hard drugs, according to Vladimir Polanecky, the head sanitation officer in Prague.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik will present a proposal to the cabinet today to reduce taxes for businesses. If the proposal passes, companies will pay 35 percent of their profits in taxes, as opposed to 39 percent which they pay now.

- Average gross monthly wages, which reached 9,676 crowns last year, increased nominally year-on-year by 18 percent, which is an increase of 8.5 percent after accounting for inflation. Work productivity increased by only 3.5 percent.
- The most popular domestic television network Nova has decided to change its broadcasting to attract younger viewers.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Unions are protesting against the proposal for a law on strikes which Labour and Sociall Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka and Justice Minister Vlasta Parkanova presented to the cabinet. They refused to participate in a meeting of the Tripartite Council.
- According to a decision by economic ministers yesterday, transformation of closed-end investment funds to open will be possible on the basis of a new law for investment funds and companies.
